about: Lab PR 244: a user's program staged in /tmp connects out to port 443, and its exec record reaches the engine after the connect (its own ring and pump: the CI ordering of the e2e). On the connect no chain fires — its exec is not known yet; NN-L-NET-008 judges the staged image of the flow. On the late exec NN-L-CHAIN-002 completes on the kernel timestamps and names the connect (Critical, primary) with R001, one kill of the tree. At the flow's close no second chain verdict (the flow ledger).

decision.name: Outbound from a staging-directory exec to non-resolver
decision.reasoning: Process running from a staging directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm) initiated outbound other than a lookup at a configured resolver — likely dropper fetching second-stage payload or C2 (TCP/53 to its own server included); kill the process + posture → ENGAGED [judged at the connect, while the flow is open (lab PR 224)]

decision.name: /tmp exec followed by network egress
decision.reasoning: Process executed from a staging directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm) then opened an outbound flow (other than a lookup at a configured resolver) within the correlation window (the exec was processed after the flow, in kernel order before it) — dropper C2 (T1059 → T1571); kill the process tree + posture → COMBAT [also matched: R001_ExecFromTmp (KillProcessTree, Medium)]
